zh.title: 美FAA資助530萬美元 支援JetZero翼身融合驗證機引擎測試
zh.summary: JetZero獲FAA 530萬美元資助；進行Jet1驗證機引擎氣流測試
body: 美國新創航空公司JetZero於2026年10月28日宣佈，獲選獲得美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）「持續低能源、低排放與低噪音」（CLEEN）第四階段計畫的530萬美元資助。該筆資金將用於為該公司正在建造的全尺寸翼身融合（BWB）驗證機「Jet1」安裝引擎與進氣道量測儀器，該機預計於2027年第四季進行首飛。
根據JetZero說明，相關量測設備將在起飛、爬升、巡航及側風地面作業期間，記錄引擎進氣口與風扇出口處的氣流數據。Jet1搭載兩具普惠（Pratt & Whitney）PW2040引擎，引擎採用頂置於機身上的設計，旨在降低機場周邊社區的噪音。此外，FAA於2026年9月啟動CLEEN第四階段計畫，並與波音、GE Aerospace及JetZero等企業簽署兩年期協議。

en.title: FAA Awards $5.3 Million to JetZero for Engine Flight Testing on Jet1 Demonstrator
en.summary: JetZero secures $5.3 million FAA funding; testing top-mounted engines on Jet1 blended-wing-body demonstrator
body: JetZero announced on October 28, 2026, that it has been selected to receive $5.3 million under Phase IV of the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Continuous Lower Energy, Emissions and Noise (CLEEN) program. The funding will support engine and nacelle instrumentation on Jet1, the full-scale blended-wing-body demonstrator aircraft currently under construction in Long Beach, California, ahead of its scheduled first flight in the fourth quarter of 2027.

The instrumentation will measure and record airflow at the engine inlet and fan exit during takeoff, climb, cruise, and crosswind ground operations. Jet1 is powered by Pratt & Whitney PW2040 engines mounted on top of the airframe to reduce community noise around airports. The FAA launched CLEEN Phase IV in September 2026, awarding two-year agreements to companies including Boeing, GE Aerospace, Honeywell Aerospace, Heart Aerospace, and JetZero.

zh.title: 國防部證實陸軍阿帕契停飛 改派眼鏡蛇與奇奧瓦
zh.summary: 國防部證實陸軍阿帕契停飛 改派眼鏡蛇與奇奧瓦執行戰備
body: 美國陸軍十月下令停飛數百架 AH-64E 阿帕契攻擊直升機，因齒輪箱可能存在零件設計與材料風險。
國防部長顧立雄表示，國防部已收到美方技術通報，陸軍阿帕契現處停飛狀態。
為維持戰備，國防部將調配 AH-1W 超級眼鏡蛇攻擊直升機與 OH-58D 戰搜直升機執行戰備任務。
此次停飛措施為預防性，尚無具體事故通報；後續檢查完成前，阿帕契將維持地面待命。

en.title: Taiwan grounds Army AH-64E Apaches after US gearbox alert; Super Cobras and Kiowas to fill roles
en.summary: Taiwan grounds Apaches after US gearbox alert; deploys Super Cobras and Kiowas
body: The U.S. Army ordered the grounding of hundreds of AH-64E Apache attack helicopters in October because of a potential gearbox issue linked to part design and material concerns.
Defense Minister Kuo Li-hsiung said the Ministry of National Defense has received the U.S. technical notice and that the Army’s Apaches are now grounded.
To maintain readiness, the ministry will deploy AH-1W Super Cobra attack helicopters and OH-58D Kiowa Warrior reconnaissance helicopters for operational missions.
The grounding is precautionary and no specific accident has been reported; the Apaches will remain on ground standby until inspections are complete.
